Quantization axis

Words: 30
Angular momentum operator OurBigBook.com
The chosen direction for specifying an angular-momentum projection quantum number. An applied field can provide a physically distinguished axis; polarization labels and magnetic-sublevel selection rules are defined relative to it.

Common eigenstate of two angular-momentum components

Words: 57
Angular momentum operator OurBigBook.com
A common eigenstate of Jx​ and Jy​ must satisfy Jz​ψ=0 by their commutator. Applying the other angular-momentum commutators then forces both remaining eigenvalues to vanish. Thus the state lies in a spin-zero sector. Noncommuting components do not possess a general common eigenbasis, but spin-zero states are an important exception to the claim that they can never share any eigenstate.

Angular momentum operator OurBigBook.com
The axis and angle of a product of rotations are properties of the group elements, independent of which spin representation acts on a state. Higher-spin generators do not obey the two-term Pauli exponential, but representations preserve the resulting rotation product. The central 2π rotation acts as (−1)2SI.

Spherical tensor operator (Tq(k)​)

Words: 53
Angular momentum operator OurBigBook.com
A rank-k spherical tensor operator has components Tq(k)​, −k≤q≤k, that transform under rotation like an angular momentum k. Equivalently, their commutators with the angular momentum operator satisfy
[Jz​,Tq(k)​]=ℏqTq(k)​,[J±​,Tq(k)​]=ℏk(k+1)−q(q±1)​Tq±1(k)​.
(1)
For a vector operator, the rank is one and a conventional choice is T0​=Vz​, T±1​=∓(Vx​±iVy​)/2​. The Wigner-Eckart theorem separates the matrix elements of a spherical tensor operator into Clebsch-Gordan coefficients and a reduced matrix element.

The operator J−​=Jx​−iJy​ acts by J−​∣j,m⟩=ℏ(j+m)(j−m+1)​∣j,m−1⟩. It generates lower magnetic states and determines Clebsch-Gordan coefficients.

Normalized highest-weight lowering formula (∣I,m⟩=(2I)!(I−m)!(I+m)!​​J−I−m​∣I,I⟩)

Words: 47
Angular momentum lowering operator OurBigBook.com
In an irreducible spin representation, the angular momentum lowering operator has squared norm factor (I+m)(I−m+1). Multiplying these factors from the highest-weight vector gives the factorial normalization displayed above. All factorial arguments are integers even when I is half-integral. This produces a consistent positive-coefficient phase convention for all weight states and fixes signs in subsequent isospin rotations.

Addition of angular momentum

Words: 1k Articles: 25
Angular momentum operator OurBigBook.com
For two subsystems, the total operator is J=J1​⊗I+I⊗J2​, and J±​=J1±​+J2±​. The coupled basis diagonalizes J2 and Jz​.

Landé interval rule (EF​−EF−1​=aF)

Words: 107 Articles: 1
Addition of angular momentum OurBigBook.com
For dimensionless angular momentum operators and a Hamiltonian H=aI⋅J at fixed I,J, addition of angular momentum gives EF​=a[F(F+1)−I(I+1)−J(J+1)]/2. Subtracting neighbouring energy levels proves the displayed rule. For fine structure substitute L,S and total J; for magnetic-dipole hyperfine structure use electronic J, nuclear spin I and total F. Electric-quadrupole interactions and mixing with nearby energy levels can violate the rule.

Spin inference from magnetic-dipole hyperfine intervals

Words: 57
Landé interval rule OurBigBook.com
Consecutive positive gaps obey νF​=∣A∣F/h for an isolated hyperfine multiplet governed by the magnetic-dipole hyperfine interaction. Their common difference estimates ∣A∣/h, and the first gap divided by that scale identifies the first higher F. The endpoints of the resulting F ladder constrain I and J. Gap magnitudes alone do not fix the sign of A or an absolute nuclear g-factor.

Magnetic-substate subtraction (nJ​=dJ​−dJ+1​)

Words: 51
Addition of angular momentum OurBigBook.com
Let dM​ count states of fixed angular momentum projection M in a finite rotational representation, and nJ​ its spin-J multiplicity. Every spin-J irreducible representation contributes one state at each M=−J,…,J. Thus dM​=∑J≥M​nJ​ for nonnegative M, and subtraction gives nJ​=dJ​−dJ+1​. Counting occupation states first incorporates Bose-Einstein statistics before decomposing identical-boson angular states.

Exchange parity of two coupled identical spins (P12​∣(ss)jm⟩=(−1)2s−j∣(ss)jm⟩)

Words: 57
Addition of angular momentum OurBigBook.com
Exchanging the factors in the Clebsch-Gordan decomposition of two equal spins gives the phase (−1)2s−j. This follows from the exchange symmetry of the Clebsch-Gordan coefficients. The total exchange parity includes the spatial state and any other internal factors: the spin parity alone does not impose the full symmetrization postulate. For two half-integer spins, even j is spin-antisymmetric and odd j spin-symmetric.

Maximum total angular momentum of equivalent fermions (Jmax​=Nj−N(N−1)/2)

Words: 73
Addition of angular momentum OurBigBook.com
For N identical fermions restricted to one angular-momentum multiplet j, with all other one-particle labels fixed, the Pauli exclusion principle permits distinct angular momentum projections j,j−1,…,j−N+1. Their sum is Nj−N(N−1)/2, provided N≤2j+1. The resulting Slater determinant is killed by the total raising angular momentum ladder operator because raising any occupied state either exceeds j or duplicates an occupied state. It is therefore a highest-weight vector of precisely this total angular momentum. The formula is invariant under replacing particles by holes in the full shell.

Words: 25
Addition of angular momentum OurBigBook.com
Coupling orbital angular momentum L>0 to spin one-half produces J=L±1/2. The dimensions add as (2L+2)+2L=2(2L+1). A change between coupled and product bases changes labels, not the dimension of the Hilbert space.

Three spin-one-half angular-momentum decomposition ((1/2)⊗3=3/2⊕1/2⊕1/2)

Words: 69
Addition of angular momentum OurBigBook.com
For three distinguishable spin one-half systems, the Clebsch-Gordan decomposition first combines two spins into 0⊕1, then couples the third: 0⊗1/2=1/2 and 1⊗1/2=1/2⊕3/2. Thus the tensor product has one quartet and two doublets. A Hamiltonian operator depending only on the total S2 and Sz​ acts identically on the two doublet copies. In particular H=ϵt​S2/ℏ2+ϵz​Sz​/ℏ has energy eigenvalues ϵt​S(S+1)+ϵz​M, generically once for each quartet projection and twice for each doublet projection. Equal numerical energies have their multiplicities added.

LS coupling (J=L+S)

Words: 167 Articles: 2
Addition of angular momentum OurBigBook.com
An atomic addition of angular momentum scheme in which the individual orbital angular momentum vectors first combine into L and the individual spins into S, then these combine into total angular momentum J. When spin-orbit coupling is weak compared with the interactions between electrons described by electrostatics, L and S remain useful approximate quantum numbers. The Landé g-factor describes the resulting weak-field magnetic splitting.

Nonequivalent p-s and p-p term counting

Words: 68
LS coupling OurBigBook.com
For electrons in distinct radial orbitals, angular coupling permits all L from ∣l1​−l2​∣ to l1​+l2​ and both total spins S=0,1. A p-s pair therefore gives singlet and triplet P terms. A nonequivalent p-p pair gives singlet and triplet S, P and D terms. The equivalent-subshell exclusion restrictions do not remove these nonequivalent terms. Counting (2S+1)(2L+1) gives 12 p-s and 36 p-p microstates, matching products of one-electron state counts.

Allowed LS terms of a p-squared configuration

Words: 46
LS coupling OurBigBook.com
Two equivalent l=1 electrons require an antisymmetric complete state. Orbital exchange has parity (−1)L and the spin singlet is antisymmetric, giving allowed L+S even. The terms are 3P0,1,2​, 1D2​ and 1S0​, with 9+5+1=15 states, equal to (26​). Hund ordering puts 3P0​ lowest for the less-than-half-filled configuration.

Total angular momentum operator (J=∑i​Ji​)

Addition of angular momentum OurBigBook.com
For a composite quantum system, the total angular momentum operator is the sum of the constituent angular momenta, with each summand acting on its own tensor factor. Its simultaneous eigenstates with Jz​ organize the state space into total-spin sectors.

Spin-one reversal under quadratic anisotropy (P−x​(t)=sin2[(A+B)ℏt/2])
Words: 71
Spin-one Cartesian basis OurBigBook.com
For a spin-one Hamiltonian H=ASz2​+B(Sx2​−Sy2​), Cartesian basis energies are ℏ2(A−B), ℏ2(A+B) and zero along the x,y,z basis labels. The Sx​=ℏ state combines the latter two basis vectors equally. Their relative phase produces the displayed spin-reversal probability. Complete reversal occurs at odd multiples of π/(∣A+B∣ℏ) if A+B=0; when it vanishes those two components remain degenerate. Individual matrix signs depend on basis conventions, while the commutators and physical probability must remain consistent.

Lowest-weight coupling of two angular momenta (∣s−1,−s+1⟩=j2​/s​∣a⟩−j1​/s​∣b⟩)

Words: 65
Clebsch-Gordan decomposition OurBigBook.com
Put s=j1​+j2​, with both ji​>0. At magnetic quantum number −s+1, let ∣a⟩ raise only the first factor of the lowest product state and ∣b⟩ raise only the second. Applying total J+​ to the lowest product gives the normalized J=s combination j1​/s​∣a⟩+j2​/s​∣b⟩. Its orthogonal combination is annihilated by total J−​ and therefore has J=s−1. This obtains a useful Clebsch-Gordan coefficients without a table.

Spin-one singlet state (∣0,0⟩=(∣1,−1⟩−∣0,0⟩+∣−1,1⟩)/3​)

Words: 87
Singlet state OurBigBook.com
In the product basis ∣m1​,m2​⟩ for two spin-one particles, total magnetic quantum number zero allows only ∣1,−1⟩, ∣0,0⟩ and ∣−1,1⟩. Applying the total ladder operators to α∣1,−1⟩+β∣0,0⟩+γ∣−1,1⟩ gives
S+​∣ψ⟩=2​ℏ[(α+β)∣1,0⟩+(β+γ)∣0,1⟩].
(9)
A singlet state is annihilated by S+​ and S−​, so α=γ=−β. Wavefunction normalization gives the displayed state, up to an overall phase. Here the ket on the left of the title formula has total-spin labels, while its right-hand kets have individual magnetic labels. The state is symmetric under exchanging the particles, although no exchange constraint is needed for distinguishable particles.

Spin component variance (Var(Sα​)=⟨Sα2​⟩−⟨Sα​⟩2)

Words: 45
Spin OurBigBook.com
The uncertainty of a spin projection is measured by its variance. In a maximally polarized spin coherent state, the longitudinal variance is zero and each transverse variance is S/2 in units ℏ=1. The transverse fluctuations do not imply finite magnon occupation in an isotropic ferromagnet's polarized vacuum.

Classical spin (∣S∣=S)

Words: 50
Spin OurBigBook.com
A classical spin is a fixed-length vector representing the orientation of a local magnetic moment. A classical limit of a large quantum spin replaces its components by this vector and minimizes the resulting energy. Its length is conventionally S at leading order, whereas the exact quantum squared-spin eigenvalue is S(S+1) in units ℏ=1.

Total spin (Stot​=∑n​Sn​)

Words: 38
Spin OurBigBook.com
The total spin is the vector sum of subsystem spin operators and generates their simultaneous rotation. For a rotationally invariant Heisenberg model, both its squared magnitude and any chosen component commute with the Hamiltonian. An anisotropic exchange or field can preserve only a component.

Spin rotation (U(θ)=e−iθ⋅S)

Words: 84 Articles: 1
Spin OurBigBook.com
A spin rotation acts on a quantum state through the unitary representation generated by its angular momentum operators. With ℏ=1, rotation by angle θ about axis n^ is e−iθn^⋅S. Simultaneously rotating every site is a global symmetry of an isotropic Heisenberg model.

Global spin-rotation symmetry about one axis ([H,Stotz​]=0)

Words: 48
Spin rotation OurBigBook.com
If the Hamiltonian commutes with total Sz, simultaneous spin rotations e−iϕStotz​ form a circle group symmetry. In a state of definite total Sz, the transverse one-point averages vanish because Sx±iSy change that eigenvalue. A chosen classical orientation or symmetry-breaking limit requires separate care when constructing a linear spin-wave approximation.

Stern-Gerlach experiment

Words: 2k Articles: 6
Spin OurBigBook.com
A Stern-Gerlach experiment separates atomic beams according to a component of their magnetic moment in a nonuniform magnetic field. For an appropriate two-state spin system, calibrated outputs distinguish the two spin eigenvalues; Stern-Gerlach expectation estimation explains how repeated fresh preparations turn channel counts into an expectation value.
The decisive contrast is between two separated components of an atomic beam and the continuous spread predicted for randomly oriented classical magnetic moments. Neither component need be an infinitely narrow spot: velocity spread and the resolving power of the scientific instrument affect the spatial image. The apparatus converts an internal magnetic moment into a displacement large enough to inspect, connecting angular momentum eigenstates to macroscopic evidence.

Stern-Gerlach experiment OurBigBook.com
The ideal projective measurement of a spin-one-half component along a unit axis n. The two outcomes have Born rule probabilities ⟨ψ∣P±​∣ψ⟩. For an input with Bloch vector r, they are (1±n⋅r)/2. This model distinguishes a mathematical spin measurement from engineering a literal free-electron beam splitter.

Neutron Stern-Gerlach splitting (Fz​=μz​∂z​Bz​,μz​=±γn​ℏ/2)

Words: 114
Stern-Gerlach experiment OurBigBook.com
An electrically neutral neutron still has a magnetic moment μ=γn​S. A collimated beam passing through an inhomogeneous magnetic field experiences the force derived from H=−μ⋅B. In a region whose field axis is approximately fixed, a spin one-half neutron has two field-axis spin eigenstates, producing two allowed transverse forces and two separated beam components after a drift. A homogeneous field can cause Larmor precession but cannot separate positions through this force.
The neutron's negative gyromagnetic ratio interchanges which spin projection moves toward increasing field; it does not change the number of branches. An unpolarized beam gives equal ideal populations. A beam prepared in one field-axis eigenstate populates only one branch, so splitting into two observed spots presupposes both components and sufficient spatial resolution.

Stern-Gerlach apparatus in 1922

Words: 332
Stern-Gerlach experiment OurBigBook.com
In 1922, Otto Stern and Walther Gerlach used an electrically heated oven to emit neutral silver chemical atoms. Two platinum apertures, a pinhole and a slit 0.03–0.04mm wide, supplied collimation. The beam passed along a 3.5cm knife-edge pole in a nonuniform magnetic field. At its end, a glass plate collected the condensed silver. Continuous pumping maintained vacuum; the thin deposit required development even after eight hours.[ref]
The field-off image established the undeflected slit width. A comparison put field-on and field-off deposits on the same plate. Microscopy revealed two deflected bands, no detectable central component, and broadening attributed to the velocity distribution. Alignment and distance from the knife-edge affected the pattern; precise magnetic field gradient measurements were still pending.[ref]
The apertures act as a collimator: they constrain the initial transverse positions and velocities, so a magnetic displacement can be distinguished from an initially broad beam. Vacuum reduces collisions that would destroy this preparation. Deposition integrates arrivals over the exposure; a darkened band is not a time-resolved record of individual chemical atoms. The field-off comparison tests whether the magnet changes the spatial distribution, while alignment checks address a geometric source of apparent asymmetry. Finite sensitivity qualifies the absence of a central deposit: it is an experimental upper limit, not a proof that exactly zero atoms landed there.

Stern-Gerlach force and flight model (Fz​≃μz​∂z​Bz​,zs​−z0​=μz​Gℓ(D+ℓ/2)/(Mv2))

Words: 364
Stern-Gerlach experiment OurBigBook.com
Let the atomic beam travel along x, with velocity v>0, and let z measure displacement along the dominant magnetic field gradient. For a fixed effective magnetic moment component μz​, the magnetic dipole potential energy is U≃−μz​Bz​. Taking its negative partial derivative gives
Fz​=−∂z∂U​≃μz​∂z∂Bz​​=μz​G.
(14)
A spatially uniform magnetic field can produce torque and Larmor precession, but cannot produce this translational separation. In a quantum state following a local internal energy eigenvalue En​(B), the more general expression is Fz​=−∂z​En​, with effective magnetic moment −∂En​/∂B. Treating that moment as constant is an approximation with a physical regime, not an extra measured fact. Assume the local magnetic field direction stays nearly fixed across the sampled beam, and that internal states follow it without transitions, as in the adiabatic theorem. The scalar gradient model describes the beam's neighborhood; it omits the full magnetic field's transverse components and fringe regions.
Assume a constant G over magnet length ℓ, followed by a field-free drift D. Neglect transverse motion at entry and changes in longitudinal velocity. Newton's second law gives transverse acceleration az​=μz​G/M for whole-atom mass M. The magnet transit time is tm​=ℓ/v, and the drift time is td​=D/v. The magnet supplies both a displacement and an exit transverse velocity:
zm​−z0​=2az​tm2​​,vz,m​=az​tm​,zs​−z0​=Mv2μz​G​(2ℓ2​+ℓD).
(15)
The ℓD contribution is motion with the acquired transverse velocity, not continued acceleration outside the magnet. For the plate-at-exit geometry, set D=0. For a nonzero entrance transverse velocity w, add w(ℓ+D)/v. These terms show why initial collimation and flight geometry matter when inferring a magnetic moment from a deposit.
Choose hypothetical parameters M=1.79×10−25kg, G=300Tm−1, ℓ=0.035m, D=0.100m, and v=500ms−1. Approximate the two effective magnetic moments by μz​=±μB​, where the Bohr magneton is μB​≃9.274×10−24JT−1. Then ∣az​∣≃1.55×104ms−2, tm​=70μs and td​=200μs. The positive displacement is about 0.0381mm inside the magnet plus 0.2176mm during drift: d=0.2557mm, with full separation 2d=0.5114mm. These chosen values illustrate the model and are not reconstructed 1922 measurements.
The exit transverse velocity is only about 1.09ms−1, small compared with the chosen forward velocity; this checks the small-deflection assumption. Halving G halves d, doubling v divides d by four, and setting D=0 removes most of this example's separation. A real pole has fringe magnetic fields and a position-dependent gradient; these require a more complete trajectory calculation.

Stern-Gerlach experiment OurBigBook.com
For an equally populated ideal pair of angular momentum eigenstates, the magnetic moment component takes two values, ±μB​, and the displacements at fixed velocity are ±d(v). Compare a specified classical alternative: every chemical atom carries a permanent magnetic moment of fixed magnitude μB​, with independently isotropic initial orientations and no dissipative alignment. If u=cosθ, the sphere's area element is 2πdu, so u has a uniform distribution on [−1,1]. With precession preserving this component in the ideal geometry, the displacement d(v)u fills the interval [−d(v),d(v)] continuously. A pair of bands therefore tests allowed components rather than merely proving that silver is magnetic. Other classical preparation assumptions would be different models and must be stated.
To include finite instrumental width, choose a normalized Gaussian distribution
ϕσ​(z)=2π​σ1​exp(−2σ2z2​)
(16)
with standard deviation σ=0.035mm, representing a combined field-off spatial width. At fixed velocity the model probability density functions are
ptwo​(z∣v)=2ϕσ​(z−d(v))+ϕσ​(z+d(v))​,pclassical​(z∣v)=21​∫−11​ϕσ​(z−d(v)u)du.
(17)
Each has unit integral and zero mean; the different shapes, rather than a different average displacement, distinguish them. The discrete model has variance σ2+d(v)2, whereas the classical model has variance σ2+d(v)2/3. Their common mean also explains why the raw average landing position is insufficient to identify the internal quantum state.
Now choose a uniform distribution of forward velocities from 400 to 600ms−1, explicitly as an example rather than the oven's actual distribution. Average either conditional probability density function over that interval. The positive-channel displacement ranges from 0.1776 to 0.3995mm, since slower chemical atoms spend longer accelerating and drifting. The two components broaden into bands even though their internal magnetic moment values remain discrete. The corresponding classical profile continues to populate the center. The displayed strip darkness is proportional to predicted deposited number density, with equal total arrivals; it is not a photograph or a calibrated optical response of a developed film.
Increasing the spatial width until it is comparable with d can hide the two maxima. At fixed velocity, differentiating the two-state probability density function twice gives ptwo′′​(0)=ϕσ​(d)(d2−σ2)/σ4: the central minimum becomes a central maximum when σ>d. Conversely, a broad distribution of velocities need not create a new internal component: it spreads each existing component through the v−2 dependence. Further instrumental limits include collisions, aperture clipping of strongly deflected trajectories, asymmetric pole geometry, and nonlinear film development. Field-off widths and a mapped magnetic field gradient are needed to separate such effects. For a modern counting experiment, channel calibration and efficiency corrections belong to Stern-Gerlach expectation estimation; spatial separation alone does not supply those statistics.

Stern-Gerlach historical and modern interpretations

Words: 295
Stern-Gerlach experiment OurBigBook.com
The 1922 interpretation concerned space quantization of atomic magnetic moments in the old quantum theory. The modern electron spin proposal came in 1925; the original observers did not identify intrinsic electron spin as the cause of their splitting. An orbital interpretation then seemed plausible, but the later spin explanation gives a different account of the same two-component evidence.[ref]
Modern atomic data assign neutral silver the ground state electron configuration [Kr]4d105s and electronic term 2S1/2​. The filled electron shells contribute zero net electronic angular momentum; the outer unpaired electron has orbital angular momentum L=0, spin S=1/2, and electronic total angular momentum J=1/2. The magnetic quantum number has two values mJ​=±1/2.[ref]
In the effective electronic description,
μz​=−gJ​μB​ℏJz​​,Jz​∣J,mJ​⟩=ℏmJ​∣J,mJ​⟩,μz​≃∓μB​(gJ​≃2).
(18)
The minus sign matters: for positive G, the component with mJ​=+1/2 has negative electronic magnetic moment and deflects toward negative z in our coordinates. Calling the upper spot “spin up” without specifying the magnetic field and channel calibration can therefore reverse the assignment. The total angular momentum operator here sums electronic orbital angular momentum and electronic spin; J is not a claim that the atomic nucleus has no spin. Hyperfine structure and nuclear magnetic moments can require additional internal levels, so a two-channel electronic approximation must be justified for the field and resolution being used.
This is a neutral atomic beam, not a beam of free electrons. The deflected mass in the flight equations is the entire silver chemical atom; its dominant electronic magnetic moment supplies the state-dependent force. Replacing that atom by a free electron would also introduce the charged particle's Lorentz force and a different preparation problem. The ideal two-state model is useful because it isolates the connection between discrete internal components and spatially resolved outputs; it does not retroactively turn the 1922 deposit into a direct contemporary identification of intrinsic electron spin.

In the ordered z-projection basis ∣1,1⟩,∣1,0⟩,∣1,−1⟩, the normalized eigenvector of Jx​sinθ+Jz​cosθ with eigenvalue +ℏ is the displayed vector. It follows by a y-axis rotation of the maximum-weight state, or direct solution of the tridiagonal eigenvalue equation. Squaring its entries gives the three z-projection measurement probabilities.

Spin coherent state OurBigBook.com
A spin coherent-state path integral inserts group-averaged resolutions of the identity between short time steps. Its kinetic term is the Spin coherent-state Berry phase, equal to S times the oriented solid angle swept on the sphere.

At azimuth φ, the normalized spin-3/2 coherent-state components are proportional to 1,3​eiφ,3​e2iφ,e3iφ.

Larmor precession

Words: 103 Articles: 3
Spin OurBigBook.com
Larmor precession is the precession of a magnetic moment about an applied magnetic field. For a spin with gyromagnetic ratio γ and Hamiltonian H=−γB⋅S, its expectation obeys d⟨Sangle/dt=γ⟨SangleimesB. A spin coherent state retains its coherent form during this rotation.

Larmor precession OurBigBook.com
The angular frequency of free Larmor precession in a uniform magnetic field of magnitude B, with gyromagnetic ratio γ. Interactions can shift a collective resonance away from this free-spin scale.

Heisenberg model

Words: 1k Articles: 24
Spin OurBigBook.com
The Heisenberg model couples neighboring or more general pairs of spins through σi​⋅σj​. For all-to-all equal coupling, the Hamiltonian can be written in terms of the square of the total spin.

Words: 82
Heisenberg model OurBigBook.com
For two spin one-half systems, the dimensionless isotropic Heisenberg model coupling is C=X⊗X+Y⊗Y+Z⊗Z, where X,Y,Z are Pauli matrices. In the ordered computational basis (∣00⟩,∣01⟩,∣10⟩,∣11⟩),
C=​1000​0−120​02−10​0001​​=2S−I,
(22)
where S is the SWAP gate. This follows by acting on each basis state: the XX+YY terms exchange the two opposite-spin states with coefficient two and annihilate the parallel-spin states. The symmetric three-dimensional sector has eigenvalue 1 and the antisymmetric sector has eigenvalue −3. Hence
e−iaC/2=eia/2(cosaI−isinaS).
(23)
This identity explains how isotropic exchange interaction generates a SWAP gate at a=π/2 up to a global phase.

Two-spin exchange spectrum with unequal signed magnetic moments

Heisenberg model OurBigBook.com
For H=(Δ/4)σ1​⋅σ2​−(μ0​B/2)(g1​σ1z​+g2​σ2z​), the parallel-spin energies are Δ/4∓μ0​B(g1​+g2​)/2. The zero-projection block has energies −Δ/4±Δ2+[μ0​B(g1​−g2​)]2​/2. Signed moment conventions must be fixed before assigning a physical opposite-charge case.

Parallel-spin degeneracy for equal-and-opposite moments
Words: 41
Two-spin exchange spectrum with unequal signed magnetic moments OurBigBook.com
If g2​=−g1​ in a shared magneton convention, the Zeeman energy of both parallel-spin states cancels. Their energy stays Δ/4, with exact degeneracy two for every field. Opposite charges alone do not enforce this equality because the masses and magnetic factors may differ.
Strong-field limit of a two-spin exchange spectrum
Words: 44
Two-spin exchange spectrum with unequal signed magnetic moments OurBigBook.com
If the differential Zeeman energy ∣w∣=∣μ0​B(g1​−g2​)∣ greatly exceeds ∣Δ∣, the two mixed levels are −Δ/4±∣w∣/2+O(Δ2/∣w∣) and approach opposite-spin product states. Four energies are generically distinct. Equal signed moments have w=0, so that block remains singlet/triplet rather than being unmixed by a stronger field.

XXZ spin chain (H=J∑j​(Sjx​Sj+1x​+Sjy​Sj+1y​+ΔSjz​Sj+1z​))

Words: 135 Articles: 1
Heisenberg model OurBigBook.com
The XXZ spin chain has equal transverse exchange interactions and a possibly different longitudinal coupling. For J>0 the transverse coupling is antiferromagnetic, while the sign and size of Δ determine the longitudinal preference. A periodic even chain is bipartite. Its continuous symmetry is rotation about z for generic Δ, enhanced to full spin rotation at Δ=1.
Classical ground states of an XXZ spin chain (Emin​=−JNS2max(1,∣Δ∣))
Words: 85
XXZ spin chain OurBigBook.com
For an even periodic classical chain with spin length S and J>0, each bond attains the negative largest singular value of diag(1,1,Δ). For Δ>1 the two minimizing configurations are alternating z spins. For ∣Δ∣<1 they are planar Néel states with arbitrary in-plane angle. For Δ<−1 the two configurations have uniform z spins. At Δ=1 the Néel direction is arbitrary on a sphere; at Δ=−1 a staggered transverse component and uniform longitudinal component parameterize another spherical degeneracy. These are classical configuration manifolds, not a claim about finite quantum-chain degeneracy.

Classical Heisenberg model (E=−J∑⟨ij⟩​si​⋅sj​,∣si​∣=1)

Words: 182 Articles: 2
Heisenberg model OurBigBook.com
The classical Heisenberg model assigns a three-component unit vector to each site and couples pairs by their dot product. Positive J favors parallel alignment. With no applied magnetic field or anisotropy, simultaneous rotations of all vectors preserve the energy, so an ordered state chooses a direction and exhibits spontaneous symmetry breaking. The vector order parameter is the spatially averaged orientation. A quartic Landau free energy describes its mean-field onset near a continuous transition; fluctuations can change the critical exponents.[ref]
Classical Heisenberg mean-field partition function
Words: 114 Articles: 1
Classical Heisenberg model OurBigBook.com
For unit three-component classical spins and energy −J∑⟨ij⟩​Si​⋅Sj​ on a lattice of coordination zc​, mean-field decoupling gives EMF​=−zc​JS∑i​Siz​+Nzc​JS2/2. Integrating each spin over solid angle yields
ZMF​(S)=e−βNzc​JS2/2[4πsinh(βzc​JS)/(βzc​JS)]N.
(24)
The constant term corrects double counting. A normalized angular measure removes (4π)N but does not change the self-consistency equation. The lattice dimension and spin-space dimension are different data.
Classical Heisenberg Langevin self-consistency (S=coth(βzc​JS)−1/(βzc​JS))
Words: 54
Classical Heisenberg mean-field partition function OurBigBook.com
The single-site average in molecular field zc​JS is S=cothx−1/x, where x=βzc​JS. Thus τx=cothx−1/x with τ=kB​T/(zc​J). The small-x slope 1/3 gives kB​TcMF​=zc​J/3. On a square lattice zc​=4. This finite mean-field transition does not imply actual positive-temperature magnetization for the ideal two-dimensional short-range isotropic model, where the Mermin-Wagner theorem applies.

Magnetization sectors of a spin chain (S=N−2k,dimHk​=(kN​))

Words: 54
Heisenberg model OurBigBook.com
With S=∑n=1N​Zn​, a computational basis vector containing k excitations has eigenvalue N−2k. There are N+1 distinct eigenspaces, of dimensions (kN​). Any Hamiltonian commuting with S preserves each sector and their population weights. In particular, a state supported in one sector cannot be transferred to a different sector by such controls.

Excitation-number conservation in XXZ spin chains ([H,∑n​Zn​]=0)

Words: 47
Heisenberg model OurBigBook.com
For H=∑m<n​cmn​(Xm​Xn​+Ym​Yn​)+γmn​Zm​Zn​, Pauli commutators give cancellation between the XX and YY terms in [H,Zm​+Zn​], while each ZZ term commutes individually. Hence total spin magnetization is conserved. Local Zk​ controls preserve the same law, so dynamics split into fixed-excitation sectors even when a particular sector is controllable.

Single-excitation subspace (H1​=span{∣10⋯0⟩,…,∣0⋯01⟩})

Words: 339 Articles: 3
Heisenberg model OurBigBook.com
For a network of N spin-one-half sites with Z∣0⟩=∣0⟩ and Z∣1⟩=−∣1⟩, the single-excitation subspace has exactly one spin in state ∣1⟩ and dimension N. Excitation-conserving exchange interactions preserve it. Its restricted Hamiltonian is a hopping matrix whose entries connect the corresponding sites. Controllability within this subspace need not imply controllability on the full 2N-dimensional space.
XY exchange interaction (E=(X⊗X+Y⊗Y)/2)
Words: 197 Articles: 1
Single-excitation subspace OurBigBook.com
The isotropic XY exchange interaction between two qubits is E=(X⊗X+Y⊗Y)/2. Its action is
E∣00⟩=E∣11⟩=0,E∣01⟩=∣10⟩,E∣10⟩=∣01⟩.
(25)
Indeed, X∣0⟩=∣1⟩, X∣1⟩=∣0⟩, Y∣0⟩=i∣1⟩, and Y∣1⟩=−i∣0⟩. The two terms cancel on equal bits and add on unequal bits. Thus a network Hamiltonian operator H=∑a,b​Kab​Eab​ preserves excitation number; in the single-excitation subspace, it is the weighted adjacency matrix, moving an excitation from a to b with hopping coefficient Kab​.
Symmetric-arm reduction of an exchange Hamiltonian (HF=FHT​,∣sk​⟩=q−1/2∑a​∣a,k⟩)
Words: 129
XY exchange interaction OurBigBook.com
Consider q identical length-n arms joined to one hub, with XY exchange interactions of strength J0​/q​ from the hub to each first site and strength Jk​ between sites k,k+1 on each arm. Let ∣s0​⟩ be the hub excitation and ∣sk​⟩=q−1/2∑a=1q​∣a,k⟩. This orthonormal symmetric single-excitation subspace is invariant, and its restricted Hamiltonian operator is
H∣s0​⟩=J0​∣s1​⟩,H∣sk​⟩=Jk−1​∣sk−1​⟩+Jk​∣sk+1​⟩,
(26)
with endpoint terms omitted. At the first link the q hub contributions add to J0​; all other links act identically on the arms. Thus the linear isometry F∣k⟩=∣sk​⟩ intertwines H with the path Hamiltonian operator HT​=∑k=0n−1​Jk​(∣k⟩⟨k+1∣+∣k+1⟩⟨k∣): HF=FHT​. Expanding the matrix exponential gives e−iHtF=Fe−iHT​t. Perfect quantum state transfer from zero to n on the path therefore produces an equal excitation superposition at the q arm tips. Since all other qubits are zero, the tip state is a pure W state, up to the transfer's common phase.
Endpoint control of an XX spin chain (g∣H1​​=u(N) (N≥3))
Words: 84
Single-excitation subspace OurBigBook.com
In the single-excitation subspace, take a connected real nearest-neighbor hopping matrix A with every coupling nonzero and endpoint control B=diag(−1,1,…,1). Endpoint commutators isolate the first transition, then propagate along the chain to generate both off-diagonal skew-Hermitian directions and adjacent diagonal differences. These generate su(N). For N≥3, TrB=N−2=0 supplies the central direction, giving u(N). For N=2 the algebra is su(2), which still gives full state controllability but omits an arbitrary global phase. A broken coupling separates an unreachable chain component.

Heisenberg antiferromagnet

Words: 131 Articles: 2
Heisenberg model OurBigBook.com
A Heisenberg antiferromagnet has positive exchange coupling in H=J∑⟨ij⟩​Si​⋅Sj​, so neighboring spins energetically prefer antiparallel alignment.
Competing exchanges on a body-centred cubic antiferromagnet (J2​/J1​=2/3)
Words: 55
Heisenberg antiferromagnet OurBigBook.com
With H=∑ij bonds​Jij​Si​⋅Sj​ counting bonds once, type-I and type-II classical collinear energies per spin are S2(−4J1​+3J2​) and −3J2​S2. Their boundary is J2​/J1​=2/3. The corresponding ordering reflections have integer indices with odd sum, and three half-integer indices, respectively, in units of 2π/a. This compares classical order, not an exact quantum product-state ground state.
Bipartite spin rotation
Words: 56
Heisenberg antiferromagnet OurBigBook.com
A bipartite spin rotation rotates the spin on one sublattice by π, converting an alternating classical Néel state to an all-up reference state. Rotation about x sends Sz↦−Sz and S±↦S∓ on that sublattice. For an isotropic nearest-neighbor Heisenberg antiferromagnet, a bond becomes −Siz​Sjz​+(Si+​Sj+​+Si−​Sj−​)/2. The transformation is unitary and preserves the spin commutation relations; it changes the reference frame, not the model's spectrum.

Heisenberg ferromagnet

Heisenberg model OurBigBook.com
A Heisenberg ferromagnet has negative exchange coupling in H=J∑⟨ij⟩​Si​⋅Sj​, so neighboring spins energetically prefer parallel alignment.
Ferromagnetic ground-state multiplet (Stot​=NS,dim=2NS+1)
Words: 59
Heisenberg ferromagnet OurBigBook.com
A connected isotropic spin-S ferromagnet with positive exchanges has a fully polarized ground state and a maximal-total-spin multiplet. For N sites the total spin is NS, with 2NS+1 magnetic states generated by total-spin lowering. Global rotations span the same degenerate space. Slowly varying reorientations produce gapless ferromagnetic magnons; finite-volume degeneracy must be distinguished from a thermodynamic statement about spontaneous order.
